content: India now has 45 World Heritage Sites according to the UNESCO website. The last addition or ‘inscription’ was in 2024, with the Maratha Military Landscapes located Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

title: Gurgaon MNC employee dies by suicide, son records video as mother screams for help
content: A Gurugram man was found hanging after his wife sought a divorce. His seven-year-old son reportedly recorded a video of the incident. The deceased's sister alleges foul play and disputes the suicide claim. Police have detained the wife and are investigating the circumstances thoroughly. The post-mortem report is awaited to determine the exact cause of death.

title: Bodies of Nirmal Purja, 9 climbers recovered after Broad Peak avalanche in PoK
content: Ten climbers, including Nirmal Purja, died in a Broad Peak avalanche. Search efforts continue for the remaining bodies after the incident. Rescuers recovered three bodies on Friday, facing weather disruptions. The Alpine Club of Pakistan confirmed the immeasurable loss to mountaineering. This tragedy highlights the extreme risks faced in high-altitude expeditions.

title: 'Ready to face death': Pappu Yadav unfazed by FIR over Ram Temple 'skit'
content: Pappu Yadav remains defiant after police filed a case against him and other opposition leaders.  The FIR stems from a Parliament skit which depicted alleged theft of Ram Temple donations.  Yadav stated he is ready to face death to protect people's faith and religious sentiments.  Varanasi Police registered the case following a complaint by a religious leader.  Another complaint was filed against the MP in the national capital.

title: 'In map of India, our North East is missing': Medallist Lovlina felt ‘hurt’ in Glasgow
content: Lovlina Borgohain said she felt hurt after noticing India’s Northeast was missing from a map at a Glasgow restaurant during a celebratory dinner. The Assam boxer raised the issue with management, who acknowledged the mistake and promised to correct it. BFI president Ajay Singh said there was no confrontation, describing the incident as an aberration.

title: Jeff Bezos warns Mamdani on NYC taxes, slams wasteful spending
content: Jeff Bezos commented on New York City's proposed pied-à-terre tax. He suggested that aggressive tax increases could negatively impact tourism and competitiveness. Bezos also criticized targeting individuals, calling it a villain strategy. He argued that government spending inefficiencies are a greater concern than taxation. Bezos previously criticized the city's public school spending and economic policies.

title: 'Should apologise': CPM slams Kerala CM over attending events during rain crisis
content: CPM leaders criticized Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan for attending a private function. They stated his visit was inappropriate while thousands faced rain-related disasters across the state. Senior CPM leaders compared the Chief Minister's actions to Nero fiddling while Rome burned. They urged the Chief Minister to focus on disaster relief efforts. Kerala Tourism Minister P.C. Vishnunadh stated the focus should be on relief.

title: 'Mekedatu project permanent solution': Shivakumar on Cauvery water dispute
content: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar views the Mekedatu dam project as a permanent solution.  He stated the Supreme Court and central government have already responded to the proposal.  Shivakumar urged all stakeholders to move forward without further delays or wasting time.  This project aims to bring both states to the table for amicable discussions.  The Cauvery water dispute centers on sharing river waters during periods of low rainfall.

title: Nuclear plants, Gaza craters: Google pulls AI tool from Google Earth in 24 hours
content: Google has removed its new AI image generation feature from Google Earth. This action followed immediate concerns raised by researchers about disinformation risks. Experts warned the tool could easily create convincing fake satellite imagery for public deception. Google stated they are implementing stronger safeguards while pausing the feature. The company noted generated images were watermarked as AI-created.

title: 'PM gave her jeevandaan': Noida teen's mother thanks Modi, wants him to 'adopt her'
content: The mother of a Noida teenager thanked Prime Minister Modi for forgiving her daughter's protest remarks. She stated the Prime Minister's forgiveness was a birthday gift and a new lease of life. The mother appealed for the withdrawal of the FIR, claiming her daughter's age was incorrectly stated. She requested stricter social media controls for minors and their exclusion from protests.

title: Meet Sophia Lee, 21, who could become youngest to visit every country
content: Sophie Lee set off on a remarkable solo travel adventure to Costa Rica at only thirteen years old. She has her sights set on becoming the youngest individual to visit all countries, having already explored fifty recognized by the United Nations by seventeen. With just six countries left, her mission is to share profound experiences while motivating young people across the globe.

title: California vineyards use owl boxes to cut rodents by up to 52%
content: A new study from California has found that barn owls help vineyards control rodents naturally by both hunting them and making them more cautious. Researchers observed up to 52% fewer rodents in vineyards with more owls. The findings suggest that encouraging barn owls through nest boxes could reduce the need for pesticides while supporting biodiversity and sustainable farming.

title: Crypto company CEO stole $5M from his own company, erased 194 records and resigned
content: Bitquery's former CEO, Dean Karakitsos, faces accusations of stealing over five million dollars. He allegedly transferred company funds to personal accounts and associates over several years. Karakitsos also misled investors about the company's financial standing and its cash reserves. Days before his October 2025 resignation, he deleted nearly two hundred financial records. The company is now seeking the return of misappropriated funds and additional damages.

title: 'Took my jewellery': Actor Aditi Sharma accuses husband, in-laws of domestic abuse
content: Television actress Aditi Sharma has filed a domestic violence complaint against her husband and his family. An FIR was registered at Mumbai's Goregaon Police Station on July thirty-first. The actress alleged domestic abuse by her husband and his family members. Police have launched an investigation and are recording statements from all parties. Further action will be taken after evidence collection and examination.

title: Huge blow! Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of Sri Lanka Tests | Exclusive
content: Star bowler Jasprit Bumrah will miss the upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka. He continues to feel discomfort in his left knee after an initial assessment. Stakeholders have decided it is not safe to push him back into cricket. A full recovery is now the primary focus for the Indian team. The two-Test series is scheduled to begin on August 15.

title: MHT CET 2026 CAP round 1 seat allotment result out today: Check steps to download
content: Maharashtra CET Cell releases MHT CET 2026 CAP Round 1 seat allotment today. Candidates can check their engineering course allotment status online using login credentials. Accepted candidates must report to their institutes between August 3 and August 5. Vacant seats for CAP Round 2 will be displayed on August 6. Option entry for the second round will commence from August 7 to August 9.

title: 'Buy police uniforms, head to Jantar Mantar': Inside 'Pakistan-linked' terror plot
content: West Bengal Police STF arrested Arpita Sarkar, girlfriend of suspected terrorist Hamim Mondal.  Investigators are probing their alleged plan to create disturbances at Jantar Mantar.  Hamim was reportedly working under instructions from Pakistani handlers via social media.  Arpita is also suspected of involvement in a honey-trap network targeting influential people.  The investigation is ongoing, and more arrests are anticipated in the coming days.

title: Market recap: Top-10 firms add Rs 2.51 lakh crore; Bajaj Finance biggest winner
content: India's largest listed firms saw market value increase by Rs 2.51 lakh crore last week. Nine of the top ten most-valued companies experienced valuation gains on Dalal Street. Bajaj Finance led the surge after reporting strong June-quarter earnings, while Hindustan Unilever declined. The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty indices climbed significantly, reflecting positive market sentiment. Easing crude oil prices and renewed foreign investor buying boosted risk appetite.

title: 8 dead as heavy rain wreaks havoc, triggers landslides, floods across Kerala
content: Kerala faces severe rain and flooding, resulting in at least eight fatalities. Landslides and inundation have caused widespread damage across several districts. Rescue operations are underway for stranded residents and missing fishermen. Authorities have opened relief camps and issued alerts for continuing rainfall. Tourist destinations remain temporarily closed due to the ongoing adverse weather conditions.

title: RBI deposit rules: Differential rates, daily disclosures changes explained
content: The Reserve Bank of India has revised rules for bulk deposits, effective October 2026. Banks can now offer differential interest rates based on liquidity risk under the LCR framework. This move aligns deposit pricing with revised LCR guidelines for better asset-liability management. Mandatory daily public disclosure of bulk deposit rates will enhance transparency for customers. However, uniform rates will continue for similarly placed depositors across all branches.

title: 150-year-overdue library book returned in Australia; racks up Rs 16 lakh 'late fee'
content: A library received a book returned after 150 years overdue.  The calculated late fee reached approximately twenty-eight thousand Australian dollars.  This rare book was discovered during home renovations and was damaged.  It was borrowed by a local resident's great-great-grandfather in the 1870s.  The book will now join the library's local history collection.

title: When a district in Florida's Everglades used robot rabbits to eliminate Burmese pythons
content: Florida is employing AI-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons. These solar-powered decoys mimic prey using heat and scent to lure snakes. When a python is detected, officials are alerted to remove the invasive species. This technology complements the annual Python Challenge, which has removed thousands of snakes. These efforts aim to control the python population impacting native wildlife.

title: Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana: How workers can avail Rs 1.6 lakh housing aid
content: In Gujarat, registered construction workers have the opportunity to benefit from financial support aimed at housing through the Shree Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana. To qualify, applicants must have been registered with the welfare board for a minimum of two years. Following the acquisition of an e-Nirman Card and house allotment, they can submit their applications. Those approved will receive ₹1.6 lakh to assist in home ownership.

title: Aarti's mother Sujatha Vijayakumar's advice to Ravi Mohan: 'be a father like Vijay'
content: Sujatha Vijayakumar urged Ravi Mohan to be a better father to his sons. She rejected his allegations and presented documents supporting her family's claims. The producer stated that Ravi had not cooperated with passport signings for the children. She also announced a memorial event for filmmakers Bharathiraja and K. Bhagyaraj. The ongoing court case between Ravi Mohan and Aarti remains pending.

title: FPIs return to India: Rs 20,200 cr injected into equities after months of selling
content: Foreign portfolio investors returned to Indian equities in July after four months of outflows. They invested twenty thousand two hundred crore rupees in stocks during July. This renewed interest stems from attractive valuations and improving corporate earnings. Foreign investors also showed strong interest in the Indian debt market during July. Overseas developments and domestic events will guide future investment directions.

title: Dalal Street outlook: RBI policy, earnings and other cues to drive market this week
content: The stock market faces a crucial week with key domestic and global events. The Reserve Bank of India's interest rate decision is a major focus for investors. Geopolitical developments in West Asia and crude oil prices will also influence sentiment. Several large companies are set to announce their quarterly earnings results. Foreign investors turned net buyers in July, supporting market confidence.

title: Bobby Fischer: The champion America summoned, and Iceland sheltered
content: Henry Kissinger once urged Bobby Fischer to face the Soviets. It was a small island, not his homeland, that gave him a resting place. In the second column of The Grandmaster View, India's 93rd Grandmaster Aarav Dengla traces Fischer's journey from Cold War hero to exiled genius. his revolutionary impact on chess, the tragedy of his later years, and why the country that embraced him in death offered the sense of belonging that his own homeland ultimately could not.

title: Indian diaspora in China flags anti-India social media posts, visa curbs
content: Indian diaspora members voiced concerns over anti-India content and visa issues.  Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami assured actions were being taken to address these matters.  Visa requirements for Chinese citizens traveling to India will be eased soon.  The embassy plans to establish a legal assistance framework for professionals.  Cultural outreach programs will also be expanded to promote Indian diversity.

title: 'If visibility is reason, then blue jersey should never be worn again': Sreejesh
content: The Indian men's and women's teams will wear saffron jerseys as their primary kit at the World Cup, which begins on August 15 in the Netherlands and Belgium. The move has drawn criticism from several former India captains. While Sreejesh said he has no problem with the jersey colour changing, he questioned the explanation that blue jerseys are difficult to see on blue hockey turfs.

title: Rs 19,000 cr investments: Noida & Ghaziabad's rise as UP's homebuilding hubs explained
content: Noida and Ghaziabad attracted significant real estate investment in Uttar Pradesh. These two districts accounted for sixty-one percent of the state's total investment. They are also expected to add nearly twenty-three thousand new housing units. Lucknow registered more projects but attracted less overall investment. Infrastructure development and proximity to Delhi fuel this continued dominance.

title: Jana Nayagan box office day 11: Vijay film nears Rs 200 crore collection in India
content: Thalapathy Vijay's Jana Nayagan continues its strong box office performance nearing Rs 200 crore. The film has shown encouraging trends on its second Sunday, maintaining steady collections. Jana Nayagan's second weekend provided fresh momentum, boosting its overall earnings significantly. Positive family footfalls and sustained fan interest keep the film in a strong position. The action drama is expected to cross the Rs 200 crore India gross mark very soon.

title: Washington wildfires scorch over 2,50,000 acres of land; trigger mass evacuations
content: Thousands of firefighters battled multiple wildfires across Washington state on Saturday. Governor Bob Ferguson declared a statewide emergency and imposed a burn ban. The fast-moving Old Trails Fire in Spokane threatened thousands of structures and forced evacuations. Power utility Avista implemented safety shutoffs, leaving many customers without electricity. Officials confirmed some structures were destroyed as the extent of damage was assessed.

title: 'We're very aligned': Joe Root reveals why Stephen Fleming won him over instantly
content: Joe Root expressed enthusiasm for leading England's Test team again.  He cited incoming coach Stephen Fleming as a key reason for his excitement.  Fleming's vision has Root looking forward to the team's future prospects.  Root also acknowledged the positive impact of Brendon McCullum and Ben Stokes.  England's next assignment is a home series against Pakistan in August.

title: 18 years after Saina Nehwal, Tanvi Sharma brings Taipei Open title back to India

The 17-year-old achieved this victory in just 36 minutes. Tanvi became the youngest finalist in Taipei Open history. This win marks a significant milestone for the young Indian athlete.

title: Railway Board panels suggest premature retirement of 5 officers
content: Railway Board committees recommended premature retirement for five Group A officers. This action targets corruption, lack of integrity, and inefficiency within the service. Two senior administrative grade officers and three junior administrative grade officers were affected. These decisions were made under the Indian Railway Establishment Code provisions. Previously, thirty-two officers were retired in 2022 for similar reasons.

title: IND vs SL: Warm-up match reduced from four days to three ahead of Test series

title: Ramayana cast fees: Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi’s salaries revealed
content: The highly anticipated Ramayana film has disclosed its star cast remuneration details. Ranbir Kapoor is set to earn an impressive Rs 150 crore for his dual role, while Yash will take home Rs 100 crore for both his performance and co-production role. Other notable stars like Sai Pallavi and Sunny Deol are also receiving significant compensation, and Vivek Oberoi has generously waived his fee for this epic project.
